mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the decision date is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financing conditions affecting corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the month prior
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns during FEDFUNDS > 4% periods are not statistically lower than during FEDFUNDS ≤ 4% periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market softness reduces growth expectations while inflation remains subdued.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market weakening with cooling inflation
failure_condition: Across 5 consecutive 60-day windows, the interaction of PAYEMS up and CPIAUCSL down does not yield a statistically significant positive 20-day forward return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 2% year-over-year coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong housing demand signals economic resilience and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: In 30% of months with HOUST > 2% YoY, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 5% predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as persistent supply-side contraction raises recession risk.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines in 2 consecutive months by >5%
failure_condition: During such INDPRO contractions, 20-day forward returns are not significantly worse than during stable INDPRO periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for the first time in a quarter, it triggers a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as low unemployment supports equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.5% in a given quarter
regime_hint: labor market tightening toward full employment
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 5-day forward returns following UNRATE < 4.5% are not statistically higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both employment (PAYEMS) and consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) with no change in inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as strong labor demand persists without price pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while CPIAUCSL remains flat in the same month
regime_hint: robust labor demand with stable inflation
failure_condition: Across 10 such labor-demand episodes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than random chance (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month decline in the GDP deflator (not directly observable here, but proxy via CPIAUCSL < previous month for 6 months) predicts a negative 20-day forward return as persistent disinflation erodes growth expectations.
failure_condition: During such 6-month CPIAUCSL declines, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during stable inflation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer confidence (implied by a positive 20-day S&P 500 return in the prior 20 days) combined with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a regime shift toward supply constraints, predicting a negative 20-day forward return in the following window.
candidate_trigger: Prior 20-day SPX return > 0 and INDPRO falls in current month
regime_hint: transition from growth to supply-constrained economy
failure_condition: In 30% of such regime shifts, the following 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
